context.title: Two Promised Sons
context.summary: After a formal prologue, the angel Gabriel announces the births of John to the elderly priest Zacharias and of Jesus to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. Mary visits Elisabeth, sings her praise, and John is born.
context.background: Priests served in twenty-four divisions, each on duty at the temple for a week at a time; Zacharias belonged to the division of Abijah (1 Chronicles 24:10). Offering incense in the holy place was assigned by lot, an honor a priest might receive once in a lifetime, if ever.

customs.note: Boys were circumcised on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12), and naming took place then. Relatives expected a family name, so 'John' surprised everyone.

watchFor: The two announcements run in parallel, but Zacharias doubts while Mary trusts (vv. 18, 38).
Mary's song (vv. 46–55) echoes Hannah's prayer in 1 Samuel 2.

people.name: Theophilus
people.summary: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1). Nothing beyond this is known of him.

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Zacharias
people.summary: A priest of the course of Abia, the eighth of the twenty-four courses into which the priests had been originally divided by David (1 Chr. 23:1-19).

people.name: Elisabeth
people.summary: God her oath, the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:5). She was a descendant of Aaron. She and her husband Zacharias “were both righteous before God” (Luke 1:5, 13).

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: A descendant of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, a chief of one of the twenty-four orders into which the priesthood was divided by David (1 Chr. 24:10).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Elijah
people.summary: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab.

people.name: Gabriel
people.summary: Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.”

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Nazareth
places.summary: Separated, generally supposed to be the Greek form of the Hebrew netser, a “shoot” or “sprout.”

events.title: John's birth predicted
events.summary: Passage: Luke 1:5–25. People: Elisabeth, Zacharias. Place: Jerusalem.

events.title: The Annuciation
events.summary: Passage: Luke 1:26–38. People: Mary. Place: Nazareth.

events.title: Espousal of Mary
events.summary: Passage: Matthew 1:18 – Luke 1:27. People: Mary, Joseph. Place: Nazareth.
